Comparison with Euclid geometry

Adopted rule: adjusted Euclid sky PA = (WCS-converted PA + 90°) mod 180°
The WCS step already changes the reference axis. The extra +90° is a separate correction.
79.3% of unflagged fits agree with adjusted Euclid PA within 10°.

Codex PA: North towards East. N = 0°, NE = 45°, E = 90° (mod 180°).
Counterclockwise on a North-up, East-left image. Pixel angles first pass through WCS.

Run completed October 2026. The unflagged comparison includes 546 fits, including 19 partial cutouts, and differs from the 527 NoQI group. Codex fits Photutils isophotes, converts their pixel major-axis vectors using the local FITS WCS, and calculates degrees(atan2(East, North)) modulo 180. It uses axial means in selected disc and bar radial ranges. These are observed sky PAs before deprojection. North towards East is counterclockwise on a North-up East-left display, clockwise if East is right. Euclid documents raw POSITION_ANGLE as CCW from image x (SExtractor THETA_IMAGE), not necessarily celestial East. Our +90 adjustment follows the WCS conversion. For North-up East-left images, sky PA = (CCW image angle from +x +90) modulo180. This reference change is ALREADY included in the original WCS conversion. The adopted ADDITIONAL +90 follows that conversion and cannot be explained by counting the same reference change again. Its pipeline origin remains unresolved. The 2777 local North offsets have median absolute 0.141 degrees and maximum 0.604 degrees. No additional thumbnail rotation is applied. We adopt the correction without asserting an official Euclid North/East reference change. Euclid source: https://euclid.esac.esa.int/dr/q1/dpdd/merdpd/dpcards/mer_finalcatalog.html#mer-main-catalog-fits. Inclinations assume a circular thin disc, q0=0. No separate disc-component b/a values are populated. These are consistency checks, not independent true outer-disc measurements.
